text:
B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yeah, hiya. I can hear you.
B: Lovely. I'm Chiara. And you are... Dean?
A: Ar, Dean. Tipton.
B: Tipton. Sorry, is that near Birmingham? I'm terrible with geography outside London, literally.
A: Sort of, yeah. Black Country. Near Dudley.
B: Okay, the Black Country. I've heard of it! I'm in Fulham, but I'm from Turin. So, erm, also a bit industrial, actually. Cars, factories.
A: Oh, right. Fiat and that?
B: Exactly, Fiat! My grandfather worked there. So what do you do?
A: Press operator. Metal pressings, in Wednesbury. Car brackets, mostly.
B: Oh, so cars too! That's so funny. Do you like it?
A: Yeah, it's alright. Steady, you know.
B: Steady is good. Honestly, after the last year I would love steady. I was in brand partnerships for a luxury label, and now I'm consulting, freelance, sort of between roles. It's... a lot of uncertainty. Does that make sense?
A: Ar. Yeah, that sounds hard, that.
B: It is. Thank you. Erm, and I saw your shirt in the photo. West Brom, is that right? I don't know anything about English football, sorry.
A: Yeah, West Brom. Me dad's lot. I've been going since I was little.
B: Oh, that's nice. I watch Juventus with my father, on FaceTime. He's in Turin, I'm on the sofa here, and he shouts at the referee and I just keep him company. I don't really watch the game, I watch him.
A: [laughs] That's nice, that. Me dad's the same. Shouts at the telly.
B: Every father in the world! What do you do when you're not working?
A: Fishing mostly. On the canal, or a pool near Himley.
B: Fishing! And you cook what you catch?
A: Er, no. You put 'em back.
B: You put them back? So, sorry, what's the point?
A: [laughs] Everyone says that today. It's just the sitting there, really. Quiet.
B: Okay, that I understand. Like meditation. My Pilates is like that, except the instructor is literally terrifying, so it's not quiet at all.
A: Ar.
B: Do you have family, kids?
A: Me girlfriend, Kayleigh, and her daughter, Ruby. She's eight. I take her to the park on me days off.
B: Oh, that's so sweet. Eight is a lovely age, no? What does she like?
A: Everything pink. And she wants a dog. I keep saying no.
B: [laughs] You will lose. Trust me, you will lose.
A: Ar, probably. I usually do.
B: And food, are you a cook? I'm a bit obsessed with food, sorry.
A: Not really. Chippy Friday, sausage and chips if it's my turn. Nothing spicy.
B: Okay, so nothing spicy, that's fine. Italian food isn't spicy really. If you came to dinner, I would make you agnolotti, just butter and sage. Very simple.
A: Ar, I'd try that. The woman earlier wanted to give me fufu.
B: Everybody wants to feed you today!
A: [laughs] Must look hungry.
B: Maybe it's the face. A kind face, people want to—
